Along with the ending, this was a solid upvote from me

While I found parts to be compelling on their own merits, it starts off very well but it ratchets things up so quickly from a bunch of bases being out of touch to a giant Greenland problem and then from there I have a hard time bridging the logical gaps to buy into the story’s world.

I don’t understand who exactly is supposed to be speaking for these chapters and the tone of the logs vs the more format-ish writing clashes as the former seems a little unserious and the latter is a lot darker. It all just doesn’t come together and leaves me with the impression of being a messy collection of ideas that do have a lot of potential but need further development.

item.content:encoded:
So when I was giving crit on this last night, I took serious issue with the length of this piece, and how it would fit in with the rest of the tale series it is a part of. I still stand by my statement that I believe this would function better as two separate articles; however, I have been reconsidering my stance on the article as a whole.

Looking back on this, I realize that the way I judged it previously was perhaps unbalanced. The article itself is entertaining and well-written, and the length befits the content within it. A lot of my judgement calls when I first critiqued this were greatly based not only how it fit in the current series, but also how I expected this to impact the entirety of the series' flow, rather than the article's merits. As such, I've decided to give it a +1, for the reasons I stated above.

item.content:encoded:
It sates itself on the life-blood of fated men,
paints red the powers' homes with crimson gore.
Black become the sun's beams in the summers that follow,
weathers all treacherous.

And here's the story of the end of the Global Occult Coalition, the only way they could ever go out at the end of days: fighting till the end.

Thank you to Logician, Oboebandgeek, red3, Nagiros, Phiiota, grigorikarpin, and Veralta for reviewing it.

Special shoutout to Shaggydredlocks, whose very excellent LITE-2712-Bosch format about Fenrir was a big inspiration for this piece.
